newsitem.title: USA: NPC to buy 100 Pizza Hut units.
newsitem.headline: NPC to buy 100 Pizza Hut units.

text.p: NPC International Inc. said Thursday it has signed a letter of intent with franchisee Jamie Coulter to acquire 100 Pizza Hut units and associated development areas for $57 million.

Eighteen of the outlets are in North Carolina, three in Texas, nine in Tennessee, 10 in Illinois, 13 in Delaware, seven in Colorado, five in Nevada, five in Utah, one in Arizona, 25 in Oregon, and four in Washington.
The 82 restaurants and 18 delivery carry-out units generated nearly $59.75 million in sales in 1996, NPC said.

The deal is expected to close in late May, subject to negotiation of a definitive agreement, board approval, due diligence and regulatory approval. It will be financed through the issuance of long-term debt and the company's existing $175 million revolving credit facility.
On April 15, NPC announced a letter of intent to acquire 52 units from Pizza Hut, Inc. located in North Dakota, South Dakota and Minnesota. This deal is expected to close in June.
Including these deals, NPC will have acquired 328 Pizza Hut units during the last 24 months, almost doubling the number of Pizza Hut units operated since its fiscal year ended March 28, 1995.

NPC, based in Pittsburg, Kan., is the world's largest Pizza Hut franchisee and operates 544 Pizza Hut restaurants and delivery kitchens in 14 states. Through its Romacorp, Inc. subsidiary, NPC also operates and franchises 180 Tony Roma's restaurants, the casual theme restaurant Famous For Ribs.
NPC's stock rose 62.5 cents to $9.875 early on Nasdaq.
